shared_context.content: Fix a prime integer p > 3. For each integer k with 1 <= k <= p-1, let I(k) denote the unique integer in {1,2,...,p-1} such that k * I(k) ≡ 1 (mod p).
shared_context.label: inverse_map_definition

strategy_summary: Reduce the global lower bound on the number of descents of the modular-inverse permutation to a local obstruction: prove that five consecutive inverse values can never be strictly increasing. This implies that every block of four consecutive indices contains a descent. A purely combinatorial covering lemma then yields at least ceil((p-2)/4) descents, and for odd primes this equals floor(p/4), which is stronger than the required bound > p/4 - 1.
